content.text:
**Recommendation: Sentry**, unless your stack is mobile-heavy (then Bugsnag) or you only want basic error capture at low cost (then Rollbar).

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Focus** | Errors plus performance tracing, session replay, profiling, cron monitoring, logs | Error tracking, with a simpler feature set | Error tracking and release stability, strongest on mobile and desktop |
| **SDK coverage** | Very broad, including web, backend, mobile, and serverless | Broad for web and backend | Strong for mobile (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter) and web |
| **Triage workflow** | Suspect commits, issue assignment, GitHub/Jira/Slack integrations, source maps | Good grouping, deploy tracking, and a query language (RQL) | Stability scores per release, which are useful for judging whether a release is safe |
| **Self-hosting** | Open source, with a self-hosted option | Not practical | Enterprise only |
| **Pricing model** | Free tier, then usage-based across several meters (errors, spans, replays), plus per-seat fees on paid plans | Free tier, then per event | Free tier, then per event with tiers |
| **Watch-outs** | Costs can climb as you enable more products, so set quotas and sampling early | Smaller ecosystem and fewer adjacent products | Weaker if you want performance or replay in the same tool |

**Why Sentry for most 10-person teams:**
- It covers errors, performance, and replay in one place, so you won't need a second tool soon.
- The free tier is usable for evaluation and small projects, and integrations with GitHub, Slack, and issue trackers are mature.
- The ecosystem and documentation are the largest of the three, which makes hiring and onboarding easier.

**Choose Bugsnag instead if** most of your product is a mobile app and you care most about release stability scores.

**Choose Rollbar instead if** you only need error tracking, want a simpler tool, and expect modest event volume where per-event pricing is cheaper.

**Before you commit:**
- Pricing and free-tier limits change often. Check the current pricing pages, and estimate your monthly event volume from your traffic and error rate. Event volume drives cost more than seat count.
- Run a two-week trial of your top choice on your real app, including source map upload and your deploy pipeline.
- Set a monthly event cap and sampling rules from day one to avoid surprise bills.

If you tell me your main stack (language, web vs. mobile), your rough monthly traffic, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
